summary: A prominent liberal political commentator has accused President Lee Jae Myung of behaving like an “arrogant ruler” and seeking to control the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) in a manner reminiscent of a monarchy. Rhyu Si-min, a former lawmaker from the liberal bloc who also served as welfare minister before becoming a political pundit, claimed the president handpicked the DPK’s new chairman and used him as a proxy to tighten his grip on the ruling party. Rhyu was referring to Kim Min-seok, who served as Lee’s first prime minister before being elected as DPK leader on Aug. 17. title: [COVER STORY] President pressed to change course as approval rating hits record low
summary: President Lee Jae Myung is grappling with a falling approval rating and no clear sign of a turnaround, as a string of disputed government-led initiatives continues to unsettle the public. This has prompted Cheong Wa Dae to pledge a renewed focus on livelihoods and tangible economic results. Disputes over policies have piled up rather than letting up, including controversies in the past weeks over a real estate tax overhaul, prosecution reform and a proposed merger of military academies. More recently, the controversies have spread to plans to build rental housing instead of parkland on a vast site in central Seoul’s Yongsan District, as well as the scaling back of South Korea-U.S. joint military exercises and Cheong Wa Dae’s clash with the Supreme Court over the nomination of new justices.

title: Korea records 20 heat wave days this year, double long-term average
summary: Korea recorded about 20 days of heat wave conditions so far this year, nearly double the long-term average over the same period, the state weather agency said Tuesday. The nation had experienced 20.1 days under such conditions as of Monday, compared with the long-term average of 10.4 days, according to the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA). A heat wave advisory is issued when the maximum apparent temperature is expected to remain above 33 C for two or more days. The nation has been gripped by sweltering weather this summer, with the mercury reaching a new record high of 42.5 C in the southeastern city of Yangsan on Aug. 2. title: Korea considers opening National Skills Competition to foreigners
summary: INCHEON — Labor authorities said they will consider opening the country’s top vocational skills competition to foreign nationals, as demand grows for highly skilled overseas workers in manufacturing and other industries. Lee Byoung-hoon, president of the Human Resources Development Service of Korea (HRD Korea), a government agency overseeing the National Skills Competition, said Tuesday that the agency would consult relevant ministries on expanding eligibility for the annual state-run event. “Because this would require a review and amendment of relevant laws and regulations, we will discuss the matter with the ministries of labor and justice when the opportunity arises,” he said. title: Conservatives voice concern over Lee's diplomacy amid growing security uncertainties
summary: Conservative politicians on Tuesday voiced concerns over the Lee Jae Myung administration's diplomacy amid the rapidly changing security environment on the Korean Peninsula, calling for stronger defense capabilities. During a seminar at the National Assembly, Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon raised concerns that South Korea could be sidelined in potential negotiations between the United States and North Korea. title: Lawmakers suggest AI monitoring to protect children, create jobs for vulnerable groups
summary: Lawmakers held a policy seminar Tuesday to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to protect children and teenagers from harmful online content while creating jobs for people with disabilities and older adults. Reps. Park Ji-won and Seo Mi-hwa of the Democratic Party of Korea co-hosted the seminar at the National Assembly Library in Seoul. The event focused on using AI to detect harmful content, including deepfake sex crimes, online grooming and illegal gambling, while leaving the final assessment to human reviewers. Under the proposed model, AI agents would monitor and analyze online content around the clock and flag potentially harmful material for human review. title: 1,138 graduates receive degrees at University of Seoul's commencement ceremony
summary: The University of Seoul held its August 2026 commencement ceremony at its campus on Aug. 21, the university said Friday. According to the university, a total of 1,138 graduates received their degrees: 601 bachelor’s degrees, 464 master’s degrees and 73 doctoral degrees. Graduates, their families, faculty, staff, alumni and other distinguished guests attended the event to celebrate the graduates’ new beginnings. Among the 122 undergraduate graduates who achieved outstanding academic results, 10 received awards, including the Seoul Mayor’s Award, the Seoul Metropolitan Council Chairperson’s Award, the University President’s Award and the Alumni Association President’s Award. title: Police bust China-based phishing ring with local police
summary: CHUNCHEON — Six Korean and four Chinese nationals suspected of running a China-based phishing ring have been apprehended in China by a joint police team of the two countries, police officials here said Tuesday. The suspects are accused of defrauding approximately 10 billion won ($7.23 million) from 118 Koreans, mainly those in their 60s and older, between January 2025 and March of this year, according to the Gangwon Provincial Police Agency. The Korean suspects have been repatriated and referred to the prosecution. They allegedly lured the victims by telling them a check card in their name had been issued and installing malicious apps to intercept calls when the victims tried to verify or call the police. title: Seoul water agency takes its expertise abroad through 5-year internship program
summary: The Seoul Water Recycling Corporation has spent five years turning its treatment facilities into classrooms for public officials from abroad, sharing the city’s water management expertise with 13 officials from 11 countries. The agency received a plaque of appreciation at the University of Seoul’s 2026 Global Friends Night on Friday in recognition of its international cooperation efforts. The program began in 2022 through a partnership with the University of Seoul, following a 2021 academic-industry cooperation agreement, and is linked to a master’s degree program for public officials from countries working with Korea on environmental cooperation. title: Seoul invites 500 dog families to walk the Han River at autumn festival
summary: Seoul is inviting 500 teams of dogs and their families to trade the city’s streets for a 4-kilometer walk along the Han River as its annual Animal Happiness Festa returns in October. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday that the third annual festival will take place Oct. 17 and 18 at the plaza in front of Mulbit Stage at Yeouido Hangang Park. Applications for the Animal Happiness Run will open at 11 a.m. Sept. 2 on the festival’s official website, with spots available on a first-come, first-served basis. The run will take place from 10:30 a.m. to noon on Oct. 17, when 500 teams of dogs and their families will walk together along the river, with commemorative gifts provided to participants. title: Seoul warns mosquitoes may return as summer heat eases
summary: Seoul is warning residents not to let their guard down against mosquitoes as temperatures ease, saying the insects could remain active into the fall and continue posing a risk of mosquito-borne diseases. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday that it will intensify mosquito surveillance and prevention efforts through late autumn as outdoor activity increases and cooler temperatures could revive mosquito populations after the summer heat. The warning comes after the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency detected genetic material from the malaria parasite in mosquitoes collected in Paju and Yeoncheon, Gyeonggi Province, during the week of July 27 to Aug. 2. title: Seoul's bridge festival returns for eight Sundays of autumn fun
summary: For eight Sundays this fall, Seoul will trade traffic for food trucks, traditional performances and illuminated nights on Jamsugyo Bridge as its popular pedestrian festival returns. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday that the 2026 Car-Free Jamsugyo Bridge Festival will run every Sunday from Sept. 6 through Oct. 25, from 2 p.m. to 10 p.m. at Jamsugyo Bridge and nearby Banpo Hangang Park. The festival has drawn about 6.47 million visitors since it began in 2022, including 1.17 million during the first half of this year, according to the city. September will focus on play and participation, beginning Sunday with a water gun battle that will accommodate 800 people over two sessions. title: Ruling party vows police reform over mishandling of missing-person case
summary: Democratic Party of Korea floor leader Han Byung-do said Tuesday that the ruling party will draw up a comprehensive plan to reform the police organization and establish a trustworthy investigation system. Han made the remarks one day after a body believed to be that of missing woman Jang Mi-ran was found on the southern resort island of Jeju following a delayed search caused by a police officer's false closure of her missing-person case. The case drew particular attention as the police are set to assume greater investigative responsibilities in October, when prosecutors will lose their independent and supplementary investigative powers under sweeping prosecution reforms spearheaded by the ruling party. title: Sejong Institute Korean test expands nationwide as demand grows
summary: The King Sejong Institute Foundation will administer its 13th Sejong Korean Language Assessment on Sept. 19 at 14 testing centers across seven cities and provinces, expanding access for foreign learners in Korea. Applications opened Monday at 9 a.m. and will remain available through Sept. 6 at 11:59 p.m. through the Sejong Korean Language Assessment website. The foundation introduced the assessment in Korea for the first time this year, after previously administering it only overseas, and the September test will be the second domestic administration following the June session. The number of testing centers has increased to 14 from five, the foundation said, as demand for Korean-language proficiency testing grows among foreign learners living in Korea. title: Ruling party, gov't stress active fiscal policy to boost growth in 2027 budget
summary: The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) and the government on Tuesday stressed the need for the active role of fiscal policy and investment in future industries, as the government eyes a record-high budget for next year. "Above all, we should focus our fiscal capacity on securing leadership in future industries," DPK floor leader Han Byung-do said during a consultative meeting between party and government officials on next year's budget proposal. He urged the government to set priorities on where and how to allocate the budget, emphasizing the need to strategically invest in areas supporting the youth, region-led growth and future industries. title: How Daejeon evolved from 'boring city' to 'city of bread'
summary: In 2019, Daejeon Metropolitan City made an unusual pitch to tourists, asking them to post their own flowchart for visits to what it jokingly called “Boring Daejeon.” It worked like a decision tree for visitors to Daejeon. Participants could answer “yes” or “no” to questions about the city and where to go, but no matter the path, it always ended the same way: “Stop by Sungsimdang — a historic bakery nestled in the heart of Daejeon.” The humorous chart reflected how Daejeon is widely seen even by its own residents as a dull and uninteresting city, a place without the standout attractions that drew people to other comparably-sized cities. title: S. Korea, US diplomats stress 'close' communication on NK, peninsula peace
summary: SEOUL/WASHINGTON — The top diplomats of South Korea and the United States have agreed to continue "close" communication and cooperation to address North Korea's nuclear issue and promote peace on the Korean Peninsula during a call, Seoul's foreign ministry said Tuesday. title: Before taking away children's smartphones
summary: Korea is moving to keep minors off social media and phones out of classrooms, but the adults writing those rules cannot look up from their own screens. A few days ago, heading home from work, I was standing seven stories underground at Daegok Station on Subway Line 3. Six elevators connect to the transfer platform, and long lines backed up at each. I picked the shorter one and waited. The elevator stayed on the second floor. Wrong line? Then I looked at the call button. Dark. Nobody had pressed it. Nobody waiting seemed to have noticed, or cared. Every person in that line was looking down at a phone. I stepped forward and pressed it myself.
